title: Write email newsletter campaigns from your latest updates
summary: Paste this week's real updates and get a short newsletter draft with subject lines and one CTA. You cut anything that is not useful to the reader before sending.

tests.prompt:
Draft a short newsletter from these updates.

Company: [ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION]
Audience: [WHO]
Updates to use (paste only real items): [BLOG LINKS, PRODUCT CHANGES, WINS, DATES]
Items to skip: [OPTIONAL]
Tone: [friendly / plain / expert]
Primary CTA: [LINK + WHAT YOU WANT THEM TO DO]

Output:
- Subject line + 2 alternate subject lines
- Preview text ≤90 characters
- Body under 200 words, scannable, reader-benefit first
- One primary CTA
- Optional P.S. under 30 words

Rules: Do not invent launches, metrics, or quotes. If an update lacks a reader benefit, either reframe honestly or leave it out.

setup.agent: Chat model; send through your email tool after approval
steps: Collect the week's real updates in one doc.
Paste them into the prompt with audience and CTA.
Edit for voice and remove weak items.
Paste into your ESP and send a test to yourself.
Optional: Make/Zapier to assemble a Friday updates doc automatically.
setup.approvalStep: Every newsletter needs your review — especially links, dates, and claims.
failureModes: Company-centric brag lists with no reader benefit

toolPicks.why: Pull new blog posts into a weekly draft doc.
toolPicks.whenNot: You already keep a manual updates list.

toolPicks.why: Richer weekly assemble from multiple sources.

faq.a: Match how often you have real updates. Monthly is fine if weekly would be empty.

faq.q: What if the model skips something important?
faq.a: Add it back yourself. The draft is a starting point, not the final email.
